observed_behavior: The original contract assumed Width By = Distance started in Reciprocal mode; explicit reciprocal toggling now confirms the mapping is correct.
intended_behavior: Smallest distance edge should be widest when reciprocal is on and thinnest when it is off.
cause_summary: The contract encoded the wrong default assumption: reciprocal width mapping was not enabled until explicitly toggled.
fix_summary: Corrected the contract to exercise the explicit reciprocal toggle path instead of asserting a nonexistent default state.
notes: Closed as a test-assumption issue after debugging the live edge width data. The reciprocal toggle path remains covered explicitly.

observed_behavior: Merged matrix-plus-sequence links treated Genetic Distance as a non-distance fallback origin, so thresholding kept all 91 links visible.
intended_behavior: Visible links should drop from 17 to 9 while polygons remain unchanged.
cause_summary: Merged links kept a generic Genetic Distance fallback origin instead of preserving the real distance-backed origins, so threshold filtering never excluded them.
fix_summary: Tracked all distance-backed origins on merged links and thresholded against the active origins instead of the fallback label.
notes: Fixed by tracking all distance-backed origins on merged links so thresholding no longer preserves Genetic Distance as a fallback origin.

observed_behavior: Post-launch metric switch previously changed only the threshold widget, leaving sequence-derived link distances in the launch metric.
intended_behavior: Post-launch switch should yield coherent visibility: TN93 sequence node-list should return to 11 links under SNPs and fasta should return to 17 links under TN93 in the configured steps.
cause_summary: Changing the default distance metric after launch updated the widget state but did not rebuild the sequence-derived genetic links in the new metric.
fix_summary: Rebuilt sequence-derived genetic links whenever the default distance metric changes so the rendered links and visibility counts stay coherent.
notes: Fixed by rebuilding sequence-derived genetic links when the default distance metric changes; this coverage is now promoted into the regular smoke flow.

observed_behavior: With timeline enabled, the 2D statistics panel kept using pre-timeline cluster and degree state, so midpoint timeline checkpoints could show the wrong disjoint-component and singleton counts even when the visible nodes and links were correct.
intended_behavior: Timeline statistics should be derived from the actual timeline-visible 2D subgraph. For the COVID midpoint checkpoint on July 16, 2021, the app should show 20 visible nodes, 9 visible links, 2 disjoint components, and 12 singletons.
cause_summary: updateStatistics() filtered link counts in timeline mode but reused cluster and degree information from the full graph instead of recomputing connectivity on the timeline-visible nodes and endpoint-valid links.
fix_summary: Recomputed timeline-mode component and singleton counts from the visible subgraph and exposed the top-level timeline controller so Cypress can drive exact checkpoint dates through the real update(date) path.
notes: Found while wiring the 2D timeline oracle. Visible membership was already right; the displayed timeline stats were not. The new oracle-backed journey now guards both the COVID node+link launch and the mixed-origin AngularTesting launch.

observed_behavior: While Timeline is active in 2D, editing link colors from Global Settings could break the recolor path before persistence was proven: the per-variable link color edit was not persisted against stable category keys, and the live Cytoscape edge style refresh was not forced after the edit.
intended_behavior: 2D link recoloring during timeline mode should update rendered edge colors without throwing, should not leave the Processing Files modal stuck, and the edited link colors should still be present after Timeline is turned off.
cause_summary: Link color edits were being written to the flat `session.style.linkColors` array instead of the per-variable link color table and there was no link color history keyed by category value, so timeline-mode teardown could rebuild the link color map against a shifted domain. The 2D live link recolor path also was not forcing a Cytoscape style update after edge data changed.
fix_summary: Link color edits now persist through `linkColorsTable` plus `linkColorsTableHistory`, `createLinkColorMap()` rebuilds link colors by stable category value the same way node colors do, and 2D `updateLinkColor()` now forces a Cytoscape style refresh so active-timeline edge recolors apply immediately.
notes: Closed after `cypress/e2e/journeys/flows/twod-timeline-controls-uploaded.cy.ts` passed 3/3 on April 10 2026, including the new active-timeline link-color teardown assertion.
